full_judgment: 9. Bearing in mind the above, this Court notes in particular that the CDA's statement in the Affidavit-in-Opposition that the impugned letter dated 16.8.2004 must be taken as informing the Petitioner that his applications for allotment remain under active consideration and to be decided upon eventually along with similar other applications before the CDA "on consideration of the overall matter which would be beneficial to the lease-holders of the Avenue" remains otherwise unsubstantiated. In this Court's view, all that the impugned letter does is to endorse the Petitioner's apprehension that he continuous to be at the mercy of the CDA's whims and caprices without any assurance of any outcome of his applications, favourable or not. In other words, the Petitioner has by the CDA's design been effectively placed in a position no better, if not worse, than he was twenty-four years ago. Such state of affairs, in the view of this Court, not only tries to obfuscate the Petitioner's claim and the blatant shortcomings of the CDA in particular in dealing with his applications, but is geared to mask and misrepresent to this Court the grounds for and the fact of an allotment already made to Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury and that too at a point in time when the Petitioner's applications made on similar terms were awaiting consideration by the CDA. Given the acknowledged similarities between the particulars of the claims of the Petitioner and Mr. Chowdhury and the Respondents having apparently disposed of the Petitioner's applications by adopting a discernible inconclusive stance, it is this Court's view that not only does that decision in the factual matrix as above cited point to an effective rejection of the applications but point towards establishing that the Respondents actions have been manifestly mala fide motivated by collateral consideration, a consequence of which has been the discriminatory treatment meted out to the Petitioner in derogation of the guarantee secured to him under Article 27 of the Constitution. Furthermore, no effort having been made by the CDA or the other Respondents through their Legal Counsel to explain away satisfactorily such reading of the facts and their prejudicial consequences on the Petitioner, this Court cannot but help conclude that even given the possible existence of a "Policy" not to generally allot vacant land as asserted by the Respondents, an assertion that this Court finds otherwise to be discredited by the lack of any substantiating evidence or explanation provided, the presumption from the recorded fact of the actual allotment of the land to Kabir Ahmed Chowdhury by the lease deed dated 10.3.2004 (Annexure-'F') will invariably be one of a reversal of such policy not to allot. Such reversal would, therefore, necessarily entail the benefit of the same to be made available to all similarly placed potential allottees as the Petitioner.
